title: Old Testament Foundations
description: The backbone of the Hebrew Bible for someone who has only read the New Testament: the narrative spine, the covenants, and the prophetic hope the Gospels assume on every page.
audience: A Christian comfortable in the New Testament who finds the Old Testament intimidating or unread.

sequence.note: The foundation of everything: creation, image of God, the Fall.
The Abrahamic covenant — the promise Paul builds Romans and Galatians on.
Passover: the event behind the Last Supper and 'Lamb of God.'
Sinai: the covenant Israel will be measured by for the rest of the story.
The golden calf and the mercy creed the rest of the Bible keeps quoting.
One chapter of Leviticus you must know: the Day of Atonement, the backbone of Hebrews.
The wilderness refusal — the warning Hebrews 3-4 preaches from.
The Shema: the greatest commandment, per Jesus.
Blessing, curse, exile, and promised return — the script Israel's history follows.
The cycle that shows why Israel needs a king.
The Davidic covenant — why the Gospels call Jesus 'Son of David.'
The Psalter's gateway: the two ways, and the anointed King.
The psalm Jesus prayed from the cross.
The temple — the institution the Gospels present Jesus as surpassing.
The kingdom splits; the long slide begins.
The northern kingdom falls to Assyria.
A prophet's marriage as the X-ray of Israel's unfaithfulness.
Immanuel and the child on David's throne.
Jerusalem falls; the exile the prophets warned about arrives.
Comfort for the exiles — where all four Gospels begin ('a voice in the wilderness').
The Suffering Servant.
The new covenant — the promise Jesus names at the Last Supper.
New heart, God's Spirit, dry bones raised.
The Son of Man — Jesus' favorite title for himself comes from this vision.
The return: restoration real but incomplete.
The Old Testament's last word: waiting for the messenger. Turn the page to Matthew.
